applicability: Applies to expressions given as an ordered list of 1 to 8 integer operands (each between -10 and 20) and exactly len(operands)-1 operators drawn from '+', '-', '*'. Order of operands and operators is preserved; only parenthesization varies. Returns the number of distinct achievable values as a decimal string. Rejects malformed input, wrong operator count, out-of-range operands, booleans, and unsupported operators with ValueError.
description: Interval dynamic programming over all binary parenthesizations. dp[i][j] is the set of distinct values obtainable from operands i..j using operators i..j-1. Base intervals are singletons; longer intervals combine every split point k, applying operator k to every pair of values from the left and right subintervals. Sets deduplicate equal results. The answer is the cardinality of dp[0][n-1]. The computation is exact and deterministic; the only practical concern is set growth, which is modest for the allowed operand count (at most 8).
